nodes.name: Inductive heating annealing
nodes.procedure: Pt(111), Pt(110) and Au(111) electrodes were prepared by inductive heating for 15 minutes at ~1100 K (1000 K for Au) in an argon hydrogen flow (3% hydrogen)(48). The annealed specimens were cooled slowly to room temperature under an inert atmosphere and immediately covered with a droplet of DI water. Electrodes were then assembled into a rotating disk electrode (RDE) ensemble.

nodes.name: TKK catalyst ink deposition
nodes.procedure: Tanaka catalysts (TKK) were dispersed on stand-alone glassy carbon (GC) disks using the procedure described previously (49). Briefly, the catalyst particles (1 mg/ml of water) were ultrasonically mixed to form a stable suspension in water. The suspension (15-20 μL) was pipetted onto the GC disk leading to a loading of ~60 μg·cm⁻². The electrode was then dried at 50°C under argon atmosphere and was transferred to the electrochemical cell protected by a droplet of de-ionized (DI) water.

nodes.name: Pt ad-islands deposition
nodes.procedure: Pt²⁺ solutions were prepared in the alkaline electrolyte by the controlled dissolution of the polycrystalline Pt wire. Typical concentration ranges used varied between 250-400 ppb of Pt. The extended surface electrodes (Pt(111), Pt(110)) were then immersed into the solution at 0.05V vs. RHE following which they were potentiostatically held in the HER region for a specific time (dependent on the coverage of ad-islands desired). Typical time ranges studied include 1-6 minutes. Following this the electrodes were removed, washed with DI water.
nodes.source_text: Pt²⁺ solutions were prepared... potentiostatically held in the HER region for 1-6 minutes

nodes.name: Ni(OH)₂ electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: All substrates considered in this work (freshly prepared extended surfaces, ad-island covered surface as well as high-surface-area catalyst electrodes) were washed thoroughly and were introduced into an electrolyte containing various concentrations of transition metal perchlorates/chlorides. Concentration ranges tested include 150-1000 ppm. Following the introduction of the electrode, the oxide layers were then deposited either potentiostatically (held at potentials above 0.6V) or by cycling between Hupd and the OH regions. Typical coverages of 30-40% were obtained within 10 minutes of treatment. For higher coverages, higher concentration as well as longer times was used. After deposition, the electrodes were rinsed.
